correctness.rationale: For fixed m coprime to 6 with at most three prime divisors, start the allowed-prime product with 6. The next two allowed primes are at most 13 and 17, respectively, within their Stewart–Sierpiński bounds. Thereafter among the next four primes above q_j at least one is allowed; four Bertrand bounds put it below 16q_j, while the current product A_j is at least 30q_j. This proves each squarefree, m-coprime backbone is practical. With X_j=1+σ(A_j), the fixed-modulus PNT in progressions, uniformly over the finitely many unit classes, supplies a prime in (X_j/2,X_j] in class b/A_j for all sufficiently large j. This prime exceeds q_j and can be appended by the same criterion. The resulting products are unbounded. For m=1 this is ordinary PNT. Conversely any squarefree practical N>6 starts with 2,3 followed by one of 5,7,11,13, so cannot be coprime to 5005. Each of 1,2,6 is practical and coprime to 5005, and no smaller m coprime to 6 can contain four distinct prime factors.
residual_risks: No quantitative or varying-modulus uniformity is established. Stored finite checks are not independent replay and are not evidence of infinitude.

originality.rationale: No inspected statement covers both squarefreeness and practicality in the claimed unit classes. The obstruction pinpoints why the ordinary practical-number progression theorem cannot be inherited by its squarefree subset. Credit applies to the simultaneous fixed-modulus existence and sharp first failure, not the Stewart–Sierpiński criterion or arbitrary results for squarefree integers.
residual_risks: A squarefree refinement of a dense-divisor or θ-sequence theorem, or a formulation in less directly indexed literature, could supply earlier coverage; no such implication was found in the inspected sources.

value.rationale: The smallest failing modulus is a natural extremal invariant for the distribution of squarefree practical numbers. The result gives both a constructive positive regime for all unit classes and a complete obstruction at its first failure, where the unrestricted practical-number AP result behaves differently. It is not a finite tabulation or a claim to classify every larger modulus.
residual_risks: No assertion of an asymptotic count or a complete classification beyond the proved regime.
